scenario.description: An outpatient specialty clinic administrator must use the clinic's one expedited pediatric neurology intake opening next Tuesday and finalize follow-up arrangements for the two referrals not selected, with input from a neurologist, the referral coordinator, and social work.

shared_context.S1: The pediatric neurology clinic has one expedited intake opening next Tuesday.
shared_context.S2: The referrals for Alder, Birch, and Cedar are all awaiting scheduling.
shared_context.S3: Marisol makes the final assignment and must record a follow-up plan for each referral that is not assigned the expedited opening.
shared_context.S4: Clinic policy assigns the expedited opening to the referral with the highest documented urgency score.
shared_context.S5: As part of the clinic's routine referral huddle before each scheduling decision, Marisol checks with neurology, the referral desk, and social work for current clinical, scheduling, and access information.

PF1.text: The neurologist's review gives Birch an urgency score of 9 because of two recent unexplained loss-of-awareness episodes; Alder's score is 4 and Cedar's score is 6, so Birch is the highest-scoring referral for the expedited opening.

PF2.text: Alder already has a routine pediatric neurology appointment confirmed for Wednesday at 10:00, and the family has accepted that appointment; the booking is in the referral desk's scheduling system but has not yet synchronized to the clinic-wide worklist.

PF3.text: Cedar's caregiver can attend follow-up only on Friday at 13:00, and Nia has confirmed a qualified American Sign Language interpreter for that appointment; the arrangement was made through the hospital access office and is not yet in the referral record.

acceptance_conditions: Birch must receive the expedited pediatric neurology intake opening because Birch has the highest documented urgency score.
Alder's follow-up must preserve the already confirmed Wednesday at 10:00 routine neurology appointment.
Cedar's follow-up must be scheduled for Friday at 13:00.
The Cedar follow-up plan must require a qualified American Sign Language interpreter.
A commitment to confirm Cedar's interpreter arrangement with the hospital access office must be recorded.
The urgency review supporting Birch's selection must be explicitly cited.

content_checks.C2: 'Wednesday' in decisions['alder_follow_up'] and ('10:00' in decisions['alder_follow_up'] or '10:00 AM' in decisions['alder_follow_up'])
content_checks.C3: 'Friday' in decisions['cedar_follow_up_time'] and ('13:00' in decisions['cedar_follow_up_time'] or '1:00 PM' in decisions['cedar_follow_up_time'])
content_checks.C5: any(('interpreter' in c['detail'] or 'ASL' in c['detail']) and 'access office' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The urgency scores of 9 for Birch, 4 for Alder, and 6 for Cedar change the expedited assignment from an unresolved choice to Birch and provide the specific urgency basis that must be cited.
Alder's confirmed Wednesday at 10:00 appointment changes Alder's follow-up from an unspecified disposition to preservation of that exact existing appointment.

Cedar's caregiver availability and confirmed interpreter change Cedar's follow-up to exactly Friday at 13:00, require an American Sign Language interpreter, and create the specific access-office confirmation commitment.
